beats: Hook (tape p22, 61:42-62:59): at 1% error per CNOT, 0.99^70 is about 0.495, so a 70-CNOT program is a coin flip (she says 60 aloud, the slide says 70: use the slide); every gate has to go right, like every stone on a long crossing (line_qc_surf_stepping_stones; reuse line_dice_hand for "the results look random", clip 62:33-62:59). Cast as in QC03-01: the programmer crosses, the fabricator makes the rope, the planner checks and ties.

Error correction = redundancy, composed the quantum way (p22, 62:59-63:24): many noisy physical qubits make one logical qubit with fewer errors; not by copying (quantum states cannot be copied, QC05-04) but by weaving them together (line_qc_surf_rope_wheel).

What a check learns (65:57-66:30): a parity-check qubit learns only whether its data qubits agree, never their values (line_qc_surf_balance_boxes: the beam says same or different, the boxes stay shut). QC08-02 does this properly.

The surface code at distance 3 (tape p23, 63:54-66:30): 25 qubits, 13 data + 12 checks in a 5x5 grid, leaving one degree of freedom, the logical qubit; the grid itself is red-pen rings on the taped slide. Check first: unrotated (25, 81) vs rotated (17, 49) layouts: say which.
Why "distance 3" (64:19-65:11): an error the checks cannot see needs three flips in a line, edge to edge; distance 5 needs five (line_qc_surf_crack_tiles).

Why it is popular (63:37-63:46, 66:30-69:36, clip 69:11-69:36): every check is CNOTs, every CNOT needs a physical link, and each check reaches only its nearest neighbours, so a flat 2D grid fits (line_qc_surf_quilt_knots: each knot tied to the four patches around it; QC03-05 stitches the same quilt).

Bigger code, fewer errors (p24, 70:04-71:08, clip 70:44-71:08): distance 5 uses 81 qubits; Google Quantum AI (Nature 2023) showed d=5 making slightly fewer logical errors than d=3, and a 2025 result went below threshold at d=7 (line_qc_surf_two_ropes). p24's plot is Google's: redraw as two dots and a falling line; numbers only via FACTS.md. Honest limit: more qubits only help when each one is good enough.
Scale (Q25-01 p12, 54:14-55:40): a distance-15 code is about 500 physical qubits for one logical qubit (line_qc_surf_teacup_crowd). The theory under all this is QC08.
Cover (line_qc_cover_03_04; for the X post and thumbnails, not a film beat): the fabricator cranks a rope-making wheel; many thin, frayed threads become one strong rope that the planner tugs.
